From: Manzullo, Brian 
Sent: Thursday, January 9, 2020 11:26 AM
To: DFP_Everybody <DFP_Everybody@freepress.com>
Subject: Social media ethics + policy reminder
Importance: High

As we embark on a new year, it’s good time to remind everyone about our guidelines and policy regarding impartial social media usage, no matter whether it’s Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, YouTube or other platforms.

Please read and save the attached documents, and read the recent note below from the USA TODAY Network News. Given the heightened awareness and scrutiny of our coverage in an election year, it is extra critical that we practice safe and ethical posting on our personal accounts.
If you have any questions or concerns, don’t hesitate to ask me. Thank you.
Reminder of Gannett’s social media policies, especially as they pertain to politics

Given President Trump’s impeachment and some questionable activity on social media by journalists afterward, we want to reiterate that we must remain impartial in our coverage as well as in our social media use. Opinion writers and columnist are paid to share their observation and, of course, opine. They have more leeway. We know that news organizations are under increased scrutiny and repeatedly accused of political biases. Let’s focus on quality and thorough reporting that brings value to our audiences. Remember that social media platforms are forms of public expression and should be used for strategic reasons to enhance your journalism, engage your community of followers, enlighten your news outlet’s audience, and promote your news organization’s brand in a positive way. Although news staffers are encouraged to develop a public personality, that personality cannot cast doubt on the individual’s or the organization’s impartiality. Violations of our guidelines are subject to disciplinary actions. Any questions, please reach out to Standards Editor Manny Garcia; Jean Hodges, senior director of content; or Kristen DelGuzzi, managing editor for politics for USA TODAY.
